title: Add ephemeral self-hosted CI runners and remote build cache to speed lint/test pipelines
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: Our PR CI median wall time is dominated by spin-up and docker layer churn for the monorepo; lint and unit-test jobs frequently re-run identical build steps. This patch introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) an ephemeral self-hosted runner fleet (k3s + runner-bootstrap) that boots per-PR, executes jobs, then terminates; 2) a remote build cache service (sccache-based artifact cache backed by Redis + S3-compatible storage) and a lightweight action to populate/restore build artifacts. Goals: reduce CI latency for hot PRs, lower runner time cost, and improve cache hit rates across jobs (npm install, go build, python wheel build, docker layer cache). Implemented as opt-in per-workflow via a new 'use-remote-cache' composite action and an optional 'ephemeral-runner' job template. Rollout plan: staged rollout to non-critical repositories for 1 week, then enable for redwood/* repos behind a feature toggle. Backwards compatibility: workflows fall back to hosted runners and local caches when the feature flag is off. Checklist: - [x] infra: terraform k3s module for ephemeral runners - [x] infra: terraform for cache service (redis + object store) - [x] actions: composite action 'remote-cache' to save/restore artifacts - [x] workflows: updated ci.yml and e2e.yml to opt in - [x] docs: docs/ci/ephemeral-runners.md and runbook for runner ops - [x] tests: integration job to validate cache correctness - [x] monitoring: added cache hitrate + runner lifecycle metrics Design notes: ephemeral runners provision via a small k3s cluster in our staging account using long-lived controller; each PR creates a namespaced runner pod with ephemeral credentials scoped to GitHub Actions. The remote cache exposes a simple HTTP API compatible with sccache/gradle/ npm tarball pushes; we intentionally keep the protocol generic to allow migrating to vendor cache in the future. Security: bootstrap uses instance identity + transient tokens stored in Vault; network egress restricted to our S3 endpoint. Observability: added Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboard, and alert if cache hitrate < 40% for 1h. How to test locally: follow docs/ci/ephemeral-runners.md to spin a dev cluster and enable the 'ci/ephemeral' repository secret. Related: ENG-4123 (CI perf initiative), ENG-4190 (cloud infra budget optimization).
commits_summary: 3 commits: (1) infra: add terraform modules for ephemeral k3s runners and remote cache service; (2) ci: composite action remote-cache + runner-bootstrap scripts and Helm chart; (3) workflows/docs: opt-in ci.yml updates, add runbook and dashboard panels.
review_comments: Jordan Lee (2026-02-13): Aisha thanks — high level looks good. Can you break the terraform into two workspaces? I want the cache to be in the controlled infra account. Also request stronger RBAC for the runner bootstrap role.
Aisha Raman (2026-02-13): Good call. Split infra into 'cache' + 'runner' workspaces and tightened bootstrap role to a least-privilege policy. Updated commit 2.
Marco Gutierrez (2026-02-14): CI workflows: please make the remote-cache action opt-in per-job, not global. Also saw flakes in npm install step when cache misses — added a retry wrapper suggestion.
Aisha Raman (2026-02-14): Made the action opt-in and added exponential retry wrapper for npm and pip restore steps. Ran integration in staging — cache hitrate ~68% on repeated runs.
Priya Nambiar (2026-02-16): Security review: ensure Vault tokens are rotated and that runner pods cannot access secrets beyond their namespace. Approving after small vault TTL change.
CI Bot (2026-02-17): GitHub Actions checks passed on re-run (lint: pass, unit: pass, integration: pass).
release_notes: Introduces opt-in ephemeral self-hosted runners and a remote build cache to speed CI. Default behavior unchanged. Ops: docs/ci/ephemeral-runners.md contains runbook. Monitor cache hitrate; alerting added.
notes_on_rollback: Feature toggle can be disabled in repo settings to revert runners; terraform destroy scripts provided; cache service can be drained by toggling a maintenance flag. See runbook for step-by-step rollback.
additional_context: We measured median CI job time reduction from 9m -> 4.2m for lint+unit jobs in staging after two iterations. Cost projection: ~25% lower per-PR runner time for high churn repos. Future: experiment with docker layer proxy to further speed container builds.
